scholarships.name: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarships
tips: Only 60 awards for the entire world — highly competitive
You need a conditional admission offer first before applying
Strong academic record + clear motivation letter are essential
Universities shortlist candidates internally before sending to HEA

scholarships.name: Griffith Global Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: 31 May (visa countries) / 30 June (non-visa) for Sept intake
tips: One of the most accessible scholarships — covers a large percentage of fees
Renewable each year if you maintain H2.1 grades + 80% attendance
Apply early — visa country students have a May deadline
Both UG and Masters eligible

scholarships.name: UCD Global Excellence Scholarships
scholarships.deadline: 31 March (most regions) / 28 Feb (Middle East, Africa, South Asia)
tips: You must already hold an admission offer from UCD before applying
100% waivers are very rare — most awards are 50%
Strong GPA and English proficiency are key selection factors
Check your region's specific deadline — it varies significantly

scholarships.name: TCD Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarships
tips: Brazilian students: apply by 1 April
Not available for Business, Engineering, CS or Natural Sciences
Chinese students must use the Claddagh Scholarship instead
One-time reduction in Year 1 only

scholarships.name: TCD Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarships
tips: Not available for Medicine, Dentistry, CS, Engineering, Acting or Natural Sciences
Brazilian students apply by 1 April deadline
One-time Year 1 reduction only

scholarships.name: Fundação Estudar Scholarship at TCD
scholarships.valueDisplay: Full or partial funding (varies per recipient)
tips: Brazilian students ONLY — this is your best bet
Focus on your vision for Brazil's development in your application
Requires acceptance letter from TCD before applying
Apply early — very competitive among Brazilian students

scholarships.name: Haddad Fellowship at TCD
tips: Brazilian students only — very niche but very generous
Only 4 awards per year — exclusively arts, theatre, literature
Programmes: Playwriting, Stage Design, Theatre Directing, Creative Writing, Comparative Literature

scholarships.name: DCU Faculty Scholarship — Engineering & Computing
tips: No application needed — automatically awarded with your admission offer
Applies to MSc Computing, MEng Mechanical/Manufacturing, MEng Electronic/Computer
One of the easiest scholarships to get — just apply to DCU normally

scholarships.name: DCU Faculty Scholarship — Nursing
tips: Automatically applied for 4 nursing undergraduate programmes
No separate application — awarded with your offer letter

scholarships.name: UCC Academic Excellence Scholarship — Masters
scholarships.valueDisplay: 20% off Masters tuition (automatic for H1 grads)
tips: Automatic if you have a First Class Honours degree (H1 or GPA equivalent)
Applies to Arts, Celtic Studies & Social Sciences Masters at UCC
No application required — just ensure your grades are submitted

scholarships.name: University of Galway Global Scholarships
tips: Merit tier (€2,000–€5,000) is more achievable than Excellence tier (€10,000)
Academic transcript is the key selection factor
Galway is cheaper to live in than Dublin — stretches your scholarship further

paymentTips.title: Ask for a payment plan
paymentTips.body: Most Irish universities allow 2 instalments (50% at enrolment + 50% in January). Always email the fees office BEFORE arriving to arrange this — once you're enrolled it's harder to negotiate.

paymentTips.title: Use TransferMate (not your bank)
paymentTips.body: Irish universities use TransferMate for international payments. Avoid sending from your personal bank — fees and exchange rate losses can add €200–€800 per transfer. TransferMate gives a locked exchange rate.

paymentTips.title: Brazilian bank loans for study abroad
paymentTips.body: Caixa Econômica Federal and Banco do Brasil offer study-abroad credit lines. Bring your acceptance letter, proof of course fees and a guarantor. Interest rates vary but are often better than credit cards.

paymentTips.title: Stack scholarships strategically
paymentTips.body: DCU automatic scholarships (€5,000–€6,100) can be combined with the GOI-IES. Griffith's 50% GGES makes its courses cheaper than some public universities even without other aid.

paymentTips.title: Work while studying (Stamp 2 rights)
paymentTips.body: Stamp 2 allows 20 hrs/week during term and 40 hrs/week during academic breaks (June–Sept, Dec–Jan). At €13.50 minimum wage, that's ~€1,080/month term-time and ~€2,160/month during holidays.

paymentTips.title: Consider part-time / evening courses
paymentTips.body: Some programmes (especially at Griffith, NCI, TU Dublin) offer evening or part-time modes. This allows you to work full-time during the day while studying, significantly reducing financial pressure.

paymentTips.title: Live outside Dublin to cut costs
paymentTips.body: Cork, Galway, Limerick and Waterford have good universities and rent that's 30–40% cheaper than Dublin. A €5,000 scholarship stretches much further outside the capital.
